answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie reputation to provably expensive identity: each agent stakes collateral before it can grade or attest, and slashing makes fake identities costly. Vouching then works like a ripple — when a new violet-colored agent joins, established saffron-tier members stake part of their own reputation behind it, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn a hundred hollow accounts. If a batch of clone agents misbehaves, everyone who vouched loses stake too, which prices sybils out of the network.
